practiceQuestions.q: In which year did Harshavardhana ascend the throne of Thanesar/Kannauj?
practiceQuestions.sol: Harshavardhana ascended the throne in 606 CE at the young age of 16 following the assassination of his elder brother, Rajyavardhana. This also marked the beginning of the Harshavardhana era.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the court poet of Harshavardhana and the author of 'Harshacharita'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Banabhatta was the eminent court poet of Harshavardhana. He wrote 'Harshacharita' (biography of Harsha) and 'Kadambari'.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Chinese Buddhist pilgrim visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana?
practiceQuestions.sol: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during Harsha's reign and spent many years studying at Nalanda University, leaving detailed accounts of Indian society and polity.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Sanskrit plays was NOT authored by Harshavardhana?
practiceQuestions.sol: Note: Mudrarakshasa was written by Visakhadatta. Harsha is credited with writing three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Priyadarsika, and Nagananda. (Option B and D check note: Mudrarakshasa is definitely not Harsha's work).

practiceQuestions.q: Harshavardhana shifted his capital from Thanesar to which of the following cities?
practiceQuestions.sol: To rescue his widowed sister Rajyashri and effectively manage northern India, Harsha shifted his capital from Thanesar to Kannauj, which soon became the political hub of North India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the river Narmada?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pulakeshin II, the Chalukya king of Badami, defeated Harshavardhana on the banks of the Narmada around 630 CE, halting Harsha's expansion into the Deccan.

practiceQuestions.q: The famous Allahabad Prashasti details the achievements of Samudragupta, but which inscription details the defeat of Harsha by Pulakeshin II?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Aihole Inscription, composed by Ravikirti (court poet of Pulakeshin II), provides a detailed account of Pulakeshin's victory over Harshavardhana.

practiceQuestions.q: Which king of Kamarupa (Assam) was a contemporary and ally of Harshavardhana?
practiceQuestions.sol: Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa was an ally of Harshavardhana, especially against Sasthanka/Sashanka of Gauda.

practiceQuestions.q: At which place did Harshavardhana organize a grand religious assembly every five years, known for massive charity?
practiceQuestions.sol: Harsha organized a grand assembly at Prayag every five years, known as Mahamoksha Parishad, where he gave away all his accumulated wealth in charity.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ruler of Gauda (Bengal) was responsible for the assassination of Rajyavardhana, Harsha's brother?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sasanka, the Shaivite king of Gauda, deceitfully killed Rajyavardhana, prompting Harsha to embark on a military campaign to avenge his death.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the political structure of Harshavardhana's empire reflect the transition toward feudalism (Samanta system) in early medieval India?
opts: Complete centralization of power with a standing salaried army only
High dependence on feudatories (Mahasamantas) who provided military troops and administrative support
A direct democracy run by village assemblies without royal interference
A complete abolition of land grants to religious and secular elites
practiceQuestions.sol: Harsha's administration relied heavily on hereditary feudatories (Mahasamantas) who supplied troops, illustrating the decentralized polity characteristic of early medieval feudalism.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary significance of Hiuen Tsang's accounts regarding the socio-economic life of India during Harsha's reign?
opts: It showed the complete disappearance of the caste system and untouchability.
It documented the flourishing trade, rigid caste stratification, and the degraded status of untouchables (such as Chandalas).
It reported that Buddhism was extinct throughout the Indian subcontinent.
It noted the total absence of taxation and a cashless barter economy.
Hiuen Tsang noted that while trade was active and Pataliputra was in decline, the caste system was rigid, and groups like Chandalas lived outside towns and were treated as untouchables.

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Kannauj emerge as the pre-eminent political center of North India during the 7th century?
opts: Its location in the fertile Gangetic Doap with strategic control over riverine trade and communication routes
Its coastal access to maritime trade with Southeast Asia
Its proximity to the passes of the Hindu Kush mountains
The discovery of massive iron ore mines nearby
practiceQuestions.sol: Kannauj's central location in the fertile Gangetic plain made it rich in agricultural resources and ideal for commanding military movements across northern India.

practiceQuestions.q: How did Harsha's religious policy evolve over time, based on historical and pilgrim accounts?
opts: He started as a devout Buddhist and ended up persecuting all Shaivite Brahmins.
He was originally a devotee of Shiva/Surya (Pashupata Shaivite) and later patronized Mahayana Buddhism profoundly under Hiuen Tsang's influence.
He remained strictly anti-Buddhism throughout his entire reign.
He converted to Jainism and abdicated his throne to live as an ascetic.
